author: "The elder" (1:1), the same unnamed writer as 2 John. Early Christian tradition identifies him as John the apostle.
recipients: Gaius, a believer the elder calls "wellbeloved" and counts among his children in the faith (1:1, 1:4). Gaius was a common name; this Gaius is not clearly the same as any other Gaius in the New Testament.

date.traditional: About AD 85-95, around the same time as 1 and 2 John.
date.scholarly: Most scholars also place it in the late first century. Some think "the elder" was a church leader other than the apostle.

writtenFrom: Not stated. Early tradition places John's last years in Ephesus.
destination: Not stated: a church the elder had written to before (1:9), where Gaius lived, likely in the province of Asia.
purpose: To commend Gaius for walking in the truth and for receiving travelling brethren (1:3-8), to confront the behavior of Diotrephes, who refused the elder's authority and turned visiting believers away (1:9-10), and to commend Demetrius (1:12).
setting: Christian workers travelled "for his name's sake," taking nothing from the Gentiles, and relied on churches to house and send them on (1:7). Domitian was emperor (AD 81-96).

outline.title: Greeting and joy in Gaius's faithfulness
Follow what is good; Demetrius commended

themes: Walking in the truth is the elder's greatest joy (1:4).
Helping those who carry the gospel makes us "fellowhelpers to the truth" (1:8).
Loving the first place among others harms the church (1:9-10).
"He that doeth good is of God" (1:11).
basis: From the letter's own text, compared with 2 John; authorship and dating views summarized from standard introductions.
